district.name: Udupi
district.description: Spiritual temple coast and culinary capital, Udupi is famed for the 13th-century Sri Krishna Matha, volcanic columnar basalt of St. Mary's Island, Kaup lighthouse beach, Karkala Bahubali, and floating Varanga lake basadi.
district.descriptionKannada: ಕೃಷ್ಣನ ನಗರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕರಾವಳಿ ಸೌಂದರ್ಯದ ಉಡುಪಿ, ಶ್ರೀ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಮಠ, ಸೇಂಟ್ ಮೇರಿಸ್ ದ್ವೀಪದ ಷಡ್ಭುಜಾಕೃತಿಯ ಶಿಲಾ ಸ್ತಂಭಗಳು, ಕಾಪು ಲೈಟ್‌ಹೌಸ್, ಕಾರ್ಕಳ ಬಾಹುಬಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ವರಂಗ ಕೆರೆ ಬಸದಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ.

destinations.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Temple & Kanakana Kindi
destinations.nameKannada: ಉಡುಪಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಮಠ ಮತ್ತು ಕನಕನ ಕಿಂಡಿ
destinations.description: The immortal 13th-century spiritual sanctuary founded by Sri Madhvacharya, the exponent of Dvaita philosophy. Renowned for the Balakrishna deity worshipped solely through the nine-holed silver-plated window (Navagriha Kindi) and Kanakana Kindi, where Lord Krishna miraculously turned around to give darshan to saint-composer Kanakadasa.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Founded in the 13th century; governed by the Ashta Mathas (Eight Monasteries) on a unique biennial rotational transfer of worship (Paryaya).
destinations.culturalImportance: Birthplace of world-famous Udupi vegetarian culinary traditions, classical Yakshagana dance performances, and daily grand Annadana.

photos.caption: Udupi Sri Krishna Temple & Kanakana Kindi
photos.source: Sri Krishna Matha Administration & Karnataka Tourism

destinations.bestSeason: Year-round (Paryaya festival celebrated in January on even years)
destinations.nearestBusStation: Udupi City Bus Stand (1 km) / Service Bus Stand (0.5 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Central city location, easily reachable by auto, cab, or bus
destinations.safetyInstructions: Traditional modest clothing required; men must remove upper garments to enter inner sanctum.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Ashta Matha administration; open to all devotees
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Sri Krishna Matha Administration & Karnataka Tourism

hiddenGemClassification.reason: World-famous Dvaita spiritual capital and origin of Udupi vegetarian culinary culture.

destinations.name: St. Mary's Island (Hexagonal Columnar Basaltic Lava)
destinations.description: A group of four uninhabited rocky islands 6 km off Malpe Beach, declared a National Geological Monument. Famous for its astonishing, geometrically precise hexagonal columnar basaltic lava pillars formed 88 million years ago during the volcanic rifting of Madagascar from India, fringed by crystal-clear turquoise waters and white seashell sands.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Historical tradition records Vasco da Gama landed on these islands in 1498 CE on his maiden voyage from Portugal and placed a cross in honor of Mother Mary.
destinations.culturalImportance: A premier geo-tourism site and one of only a few places on Earth with such well-defined columnar volcanic formations right on a tropical beach.

photos.caption: St. Mary's Island (Hexagonal Columnar Basaltic Lava)
photos.source: Geological Survey of India & Malpe Beach Development Committee

destinations.bestSeason: October to May (Ferry service suspended during monsoon from June to September)
destinations.openingHours: 09:00 – 17:30 (Ferry boats operate from Malpe Sea Walk / Beach)
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 6 km ferry ride from Malpe, 12 km from Udupi
destinations.roadAccessibility: Drive to Malpe Beach, then board authorized tourist ferry boats
destinations.safetyInstructions: Swimming is strictly prohibited off the island due to strong underwater rip currents and sharp basalt edges. Strictly zero-plastic island.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Ferry boat ticket from Malpe port counters includes island conservation fee
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Geological Survey of India & Malpe Beach Development Committee

destinations.name: Varanga Kere Basadi (Lake Jain Temple)
destinations.description: An idyllic 12th-century Jain basadi (Kere Basadi / Chaturmukha Basadi) resting serenely in the exact center of a tranquil 14-acre natural lake surrounded by pink water lilies. Accessible only by a wooden rowboat poled by a temple boatman, enshrining four Tirthankaras facing the cardinal directions.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Built by the Alupa dynasty queen in the 12th century; renowned for ancient Kannada stone inscriptions and peaceful water solitude.
destinations.culturalImportance: One of coastal Karnataka's most serene and photogenic hidden spiritual gems, free from commercial bustle.
destinations.bestSeason: October to March (Water lilies bloom in abundance)
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 25 km from Karkala, 38 km from Udupi
destinations.nearestBusStation: Varanga Cross Bus Stop (0.5 km) / Hebri Bus Stand (10 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved state road connecting Udupi, Karkala, and Agumbe
destinations.safetyInstructions: Life vests provided on the short rowboat crossing. Do not pluck water lilies from the lake.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Local Jain Mutt management; small boat fee (₹20)

hiddenGemClassification.reason: Unique 12th-century Jain basadi floating in the center of a lotus lake, reached by wooden boat.
